messages:
maya: quick thought — instead of a separate manifest file for shard offsets, what if each shard file had a small TLV header (magic, version, checksum, index entries) so range GETs can start streaming immediately?
leo: I like the range-friendly angle. TLV per-shard means clients can open a single shard and read metadata without hitting a central index. fewer round trips. :thumbsup:
samir: downside: updating metadata (e.g., replacing shard) becomes trickier — need atomic replace or write-new-then-swap to avoid partial headers. also increases per-file overhead for tiny shards.
irene: another tradeoff: verification. If header contains a merkle-ish chunk table we can checksum individual pieces during warmup and accept partial availability. that helps degraded-mode serving.
maya: exactly. Proposal sketch: header(64 bytes) -> chunk-index (N entries) -> payload. chunk-index entries are (offset,len,crc32). runtime can fetch chunk-by-chunk and validate before mapping to GPU.
leo: how many chunks per shard? big parameter. if chunks are too small we pay more requests; too big and we lose parallelism for prefetch. maybe size tied to preferred devext batching window (like 4MB chunks)?
samir: also consider lazy quantization: store float16 base shards and small quant metadata to do on-the-fly quantize-to-int8 during warmup. header could point to a quant-table blob. that avoids maintaining multiple copies.
irene: but on-the-fly quantization on CPU during warmup might spike host CPU and delay warmup. would need background workers and backpressure. Also we'd have to store quant params deterministically to ensure identical outputs across hosts.
maya: agreed. we can make quantization optional per-deployment. header flags: prequantized, quant-table-ref, streaming-friendly. runtime picks fallback.
leo: what about compatibility with safetensors? can we embed this TLV header while keeping the safetensors payload intact so higher-level tooling still reads it?
samir: probably: put TLV before the safetensors blob and update readers that expect byte offsets. But that means existing safetensors tools would break unless TLV is a recognized preface. Could instead put a tiny index file alongside with same basename + .idx.
irene: index file has centralization problem again but it's easier to roll out incrementally. clients that understand .idx can stream; others ignore.
maya: ops question: when doing hot-swaps (model rollback) we need to ensure no client is mid-stream reading the old shard while FS rename happens. Suggest atomic renames and versioned filenames: model-v42/shard-0.bin. replace by writing model-v43/..., then switch a symlink.
leo: cloud object stores don't have atomic renames. For S3, need manifest-level pointer update with strong consistency guarantees. so header-in-file helps because readers can verify they have correct version via header.version.
samir: build-bot: perf experiment logs?
build-bot: recent run (run-2026-03-18): streaming shards with 4MB chunk-index reduced tail latency by ~18% compared to whole-file fetch on our 1k token traces. CPU overhead for crc checks ~2% of host CPU.
irene: great data. next steps: write RFC stub with pros/cons for: per-shard TLV header vs sidecar .idx, chunk size tuning, lazy-quant workflow, and rollout strategy for safeguarding atomicity on object stores.
maya: I'll draft the RFC and include a small compatibility shim for safetensors (prefix marker) so old tools can skip safely. tagging @leo @samir for review.
leo: thanks — I'll sketch the chunk sizing sim and add numbers.
samir: will enumerate failure modes (partial writes, corrupted headers, mid-read swaps).
irene: I'll add ops checklist for S3 vs local FS deployments.
maya: cool. closing loop: aim to have draft by EOD tomorrow. :spiral_calendar:
